title: أَسْمَاءُ الْإِشَارَةِ
blocks: Demonstratives help you point to people and things, identify objects, describe places and make your meaning precise.
## Use the chapter at the depth you need
- Explain definiteness in demonstrative noun phrases.

TABLE: Meaning | Form | Use | Example // this | هٰذَا | masculine singular | هٰذَا طَالِبٌ. // this | هٰذِهِ | feminine singular | هٰذِهِ طَالِبَةٌ. // these | هٰؤُلَاءِ | human plural, male, female or mixed | هٰؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ.
[callout] Key point: Arabic does not use one single word for “this”. You must choose according to the grammatical gender of the noun.

TABLE: Meaning | Form | Use | Example // that | ذٰلِكَ | masculine singular | ذٰلِكَ بَيْتٌ. // that | تِلْكَ | feminine singular | تِلْكَ مَدْرَسَةٌ. // those | أُولٰئِكَ | human plural | أُولٰئِكَ مُعَلِّمُونَ.
[callout] Pronunciation note: the dagger alif in forms such as هٰذَا and ذٰلِكَ represents a long ā sound, even though it is not written as an ordinary alif.
[example] هٰذَا كِتَابٌ جَدِيدٌ. This is a new book.
[example] هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ. This is a new bag.
[example] هٰؤُلَاءِ طَالِبَاتٌ مُجْتَهِدَاتٌ. These are hardworking female students.
[callout] Important non-human plural rule: non-human plurals are usually treated grammatically as feminine singular. Therefore Arabic commonly uses هٰذِهِ or تِلْكَ with them.
[example] هٰذِهِ كُتُبٌ مُفِيدَةٌ. These are useful books.
[example] تِلْكَ سَيَّارَاتٌ سَرِيعَةٌ. Those are fast cars.

TABLE: Meaning | Nominative | Accusative / genitive | Example // these two — masculine | هٰذَانِ | هٰذَيْنِ | هٰذَانِ طَالِبَانِ. // these two — feminine | هَاتَانِ | هَاتَيْنِ | هَاتَانِ طَالِبَتَانِ. // those two — masculine | ذَانِكَ | ذَيْنِكَ | ذَانِكَ طَالِبَانِ. // those two — feminine | تَانِكَ | تَيْنِكَ | تَانِكَ طَالِبَتَانِ.
[callout] Revision boundary: dual forms are valuable extra support. Students should first secure the core singular and plural forms before studying case changes.

[ar] هٰذَا مَتْحَفٌ جَدِيدٌ، وَهٰذِهِ قَاعَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ. هٰؤُلَاءِ زُوَّارٌ مِنْ بِلَادٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ. فِي آخِرِ الْقَاعَةِ تِلْكَ صُورٌ قَدِيمَةٌ، وَذٰلِكَ تِمْثَالٌ مَشْهُورٌ. أُولٰئِكَ مُرْشِدُونَ يَشْرَحُونَ تَارِيخَ الْمَكَانِ.

This is a new museum, and this is a large hall. These are visitors from different countries. At the end of the hall, those are old pictures, and that is a famous statue. Those are guides explaining the history of the place.

## Why this grammar matters for confident Arabic communication
Demonstratives help identify which person, place or object a speaker means.
Students must track reference across descriptions, notices and narratives.
They support descriptions of pictures, places, people and objects.
They make descriptions more precise and reduce repetition.

## Common mistakes and how to repair them
Non-human plurals normally take feminine singular agreement.
Use the near form when the object is close.
